name: The Weird Internet
author: Multiverse Video editors
description: Celebrate creative computing, independent culture, and genuinely strange ideas.

items.note: Artist bleeptrack's workshop on coding your own generative art with paper.js, from first shape to a piece that surprises you.
Build a chatbot character inside a Godot game that talks to a language model running on your own machine through Ollama.
Rhizome's panel on the ethics of archiving digital folklore: memes, image macros, and who gets a say when the web's culture is preserved.
Nine iterations of one creative-coding sketch in OPENRNDR, showing how an idea evolves rather than just the finished piece.
From the Blender Conference 2026: procedural workflows with Gaussian splatting, the new way to turn photos into 3D scenes.
Rhizome's Net Art Anthology on distribution and disappearance after 9/11: how net art changed as the web did. Captioned.
Artist Špela Petrič presents The Archive of In-Operables, made during a residency at Waag Futurelab: strange, thoughtful art at the edge of biology and tech.
A short Demoscene Report: what the demoscene released and celebrated this fortnight, from a long-running scener. Captioned.
A talk on 3D printing with mycelium: growing structures from fungus instead of plastic.
A 2024 demo that squeezes astonishing effects out of a stock 8 MHz Atari STE: the demoscene's art of doing impossible things with old hardware.
A Stargate-inspired 'Dial-Home Device' built from scratch: a beautifully unnecessary machine, documented build step by build step.
A review of Writing Interactive Fiction With Twine, a friendly on-ramp into making playable stories.
